measured_mechanism.why_it_shreds: read off page 38's own get_text('dict'): every fragment is its own PyMuPDF line, dir=(0.0,-1.0), all with x-extent 491.8..503.7 (one column), y-extents butting against each other (94.5..113.7, 113.7..122.8, 122.5..130.1, 135.3..165.1). PyMuPDF starts a new line whenever the next glyph run is not ahead of the current one along the writing direction; this caption's runs are placed behind each other, so it is cut at every run boundary and emitted in y-order, i.e. reversed.

page_derived_quantities: perpendicular overlap of two lines' bboxes = 'same baseline column' (from the page's own line geometry)
separation along the text direction between two lines (from the page's own line geometry)
the thinner line's own perpendicular extent = that line's glyph height ON THIS PAGE, used as the largest separation that can still be an inter-word space rather than a line break
shred_test_derivation.verdict: spurious > genuine -- a comparison between two counts the page itself produces. No numeric threshold, nothing calibrated against a corpus. <2 comparable lines returns False (#145 absence-of-evidence rule).
shred_test_derivation.rejected_alternative: the issue's suggested 'fraction of one-/two-character lines'. Measured over the 11 rotated born-digital pages of the 27-paper reference corpus it cannot separate the defect from a chart: pflueger_rinaldi p37 has 67 short lines out of 95 and is perfectly sound (axis tick labels '0 5 10 15 20', caption reads back verbatim); p38 57/106; p39 65/111. The geometric test fires on 1 of the 11, and on exactly 1 page across all 27 papers.
shred_test_derivation.corpus_sweep_after_fix: pages flagged across the 27-paper reference corpus: [('kaminska_mumtaz_sustek', 38)]

remedy.png: orchestrator._render_d3_floor_png parameterised with stem/label so the #263 floor writes shredded_rotated_page_pN.png and cannot overwrite the TR-3 table floor's PNG

disagreement_with_brief: The shred check runs on the no-table branch only. This is NOT a re-narrowing to has_tables: rotation is now consulted on both branches, and on a rotated page WITH a table the GH-147 branch already refuses unconditionally, which is strictly stronger. It is also the honest limit of the predicate -- a rotated table's cells legitimately tile along the reading axis, the exact geometry the shred test reads as damage. Measured on the existing _rotated_ruled_grid_pdf fixture: spurious 9, genuine 5, i.e. it would fire. Running it there would convert that page's existing WARNING-with-prose into an ERROR floor, a behaviour change #263 does not ask for and that test_landscape_refusal_a2_gh147.py correctly pins against.
